skill.name: repro-first-debugging
skill.description: Debug by reproducing the failure first, then forming and testing hypotheses before editing code. Use when asked to fix a bug, a failing test, a crash or unexpected behavior.
skill.summary: Reproduce failures, test competing hypotheses, apply focused fixes, and report verification evidence.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting or ordinary debugging prose. No evidence found of malicious execution, reconnaissance, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. The skill describes a reproduction-first debugging workflow with explicit verification and scope limits.

static_findings.snippet: 5. **Test the hypotheses, cheapest first.** Read the code path, add temporary logging or assertions,
8. **Look for siblings.** Search for the same pattern elsewhere (`rg`) and report, but do not change
Goal: fix the cause, prove the fix, and avoid editing on a guess.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:20 uses Markdown inline backticks around git bisect and git log examples within a debugging checklist. These are relevant debugging operations, not Ruby execution or shell command substitution.
SKILL.md:23 uses Markdown backticks to name rg for finding similar code. It explicitly limits changes to related code and contains no executable backtick expression.
SKILL.md:27-35 is a Markdown fenced report template containing descriptive placeholders. The fence does not execute code or invoke a shell.
SKILL.md:12 states the goal of fixing causes and proving fixes before speculative edits. It requests no system enumeration, sensitive information, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Speculative fixes can hide causes and leave bugs unresolved. This skill guides assistants through reproduction, hypothesis testing, focused changes, and evidence-based verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides assistants to restate expected and actual behavior and request missing reproduction details.
Directs assistants to reproduce failures and reduce them to minimal inputs or automated tests.
Structures two or three hypotheses with supporting checks ranked by likelihood and cost.
Suggests code inspection, temporary logging, assertions, and Git history checks to test hypotheses.
Requires focused fixes, before-and-after verification, and searches for related issues without unrelated edits.
Provides a report format covering failure, reproduction, root cause, evidence, fix, verification, and related risks.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not a standalone debugger, test runner, or executable script.
Requires access to relevant code, reproduction inputs, and a working execution environment.
Stops when reproduction fails unless the user explicitly requests a blind fix.
Stops after three failed hypotheses and reports missing evidence instead of guaranteeing a solution.

use_cases.title: Repair a failing test
use_cases.description: Reproduce a regression, compare possible causes, and verify a focused fix against the original test and nearby tests.

use_cases.title: Reduce a bug report
use_cases.description: Turn a complex failure into a minimal input or automated regression test with clear expected and actual behavior.

use_cases.title: Investigate a recurring defect
use_cases.description: Trace evidence through code and recent changes, then report similar patterns without expanding the patch scope.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use repro-first-debugging for this bug: [symptom]. Expected behavior: [expected]. Actual behavior: [actual]. Ask for missing reproduction details before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: describe a bug and establish a reproducible starting point.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a reproducible test failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use repro-first-debugging on [failing test command]. Capture the failure, list plausible causes, make the smallest supported fix, and show verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: repair a failure with an existing test command.

prompt_templates.title: Minimize a complex reproduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [failure] using [steps or input]. Reduce the reproduction, add a regression test, compare three hypotheses, and remove temporary diagnostics after verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: isolate a failure with multiple possible causes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a historical regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the regression between [known good revision] and [failing revision] in an isolated checkout. Reproduce first, test hypotheses, and report evidence and related risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: use revision history to investigate a regression without disturbing active work.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: an empty search returns an error instead of an empty result list.
output: Failure: empty searches should return an empty list, but the regression test reports an exception.
Reproduction: the focused empty-search test fails consistently.
Root cause: result processing assumes at least one entry exists.
Evidence: the empty-input case fails while the single-result case passes.
Fix: handle empty results before reading the first entry.
Verification: the original failing test and nearby search tests pass after the change.
Related risks: a similar assumption was found elsewhere and reported without edits.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: investigate an intermittent export crash that does not occur in the available environment.
output: Failure: an export sometimes crashes instead of completing.
Reproduction: repeated attempts with the supplied input did not trigger the reported crash.
Fix: no code changes made because reproduction did not succeed.
Next evidence needed: exact error output, triggering input, and environment details from a failing run.

best_practices: Provide exact failure output, reproduction steps, and expected behavior before requesting a fix.
Preserve a minimal failing test and record evidence for each hypothesis.
Use an isolated checkout for history investigations and report before-and-after test commands with their results.
anti_patterns: Requesting speculative edits before reproducing the reported failure.
Deleting or weakening tests to produce a passing result.
Expanding the patch to unrelated code or claiming success without verification.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a structured debugging workflow and report format. It does not include an executable debugger.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running tests still requires suitable tools and project access.

faq.question: What happens when the failure cannot be reproduced?
faq.answer: The assistant should stop and report attempted reproductions. The skill permits a blind fix only when the user explicitly requests one.

faq.question: What happens after three hypotheses fail?
faq.answer: The assistant should stop and report established facts and missing evidence.

faq.question: Does it require a particular programming language?
faq.answer: No specific language is required. The workflow uses the project test framework and available debugging tools.

faq.question: How should a completed fix be verified?
faq.answer: Show a command that failed before and passes afterward. Run nearby tests and the full suite when it is fast.
